 Order
Date : 04.12.2025 Heard Ms. T. Jini, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the
applicant/appellant-State.
Office Note dated 10.11.2025 reflects that service in respect of respondent No. 2 has been
received.
The Office Note dated 10.10.2025 further reflects that respondents No. 1, 3, 4 and 5 have also received the service.
In view of the above, notice upon all the respondents are completed.
However, none has appeared on behalf of the respondents.

This is an application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963, praying for condonation of delay of 190 days in preferring the connected appeal against the judgment and order dated 04.03.2022, passed by the learned Page No.# 3/3 Special Judge (POCSO), Tezu, in POCSO Case No.24(NMS)/2019, under Sections 328/342/376(3) of the IPC read with Section 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012, whereby all the accused persons have been acquitted.

The learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the applicant-State submits that the delay in filing the connected appeal occurred during the process of official procedures, and the reasons therefor, have been explained in paragraphs 2, 3 and 4 of the application.

Upon consideration of the explanation given in the aforesaid paragraphs, this Court is of the view that the applicant/appellant was prevented by a sufficient cause in not preferring the connected appeal within the stipulated time.

In view of the above, the delay of 190 days in filing the connected appeal is hereby condoned.
With the above, the I.A.(Crl.) stands allowed and disposed of.
